core.title: Declare each user/system flow's themes explicitly, primary theme first
core.given: A user/system flow groups themed product capabilities and may not yet declare a themes list.
core.when: You create a user/system flow, touch one lacking an explicit themes list, change its themes or their order, add/remove/move its product capabilities, or re-theme a member product capability.
core.then: The user/system flow declares its themes explicitly as a list whose first entry is its primary theme.
prefer: Most product capabilities should match the primary (first declared) theme; keep it so when adding, moving or re-theming product capabilities.
For a user/system flow spanning multiple themes, list the dominant theme first, others after as secondary.
On a move, recheck both the user/system flow left and the user/system flow joined.
avoid: Themes only implied by the user/system flow's name or product capabilities.
Letting most product capabilities drift to a secondary or undeclared theme.
Listing many secondary themes just to make off-theme product capabilities look aligned.
unless: Secondary themes are allowed when a user/system flow spans multiple themes; not every product capability needs to match the primary.
core.why: The primary theme is the first declared theme, so it exists only if themes are declared explicitly; most product capabilities matching it keeps the user/system flow coherent.
evidence: Each affected user/system flow has an explicit, non-empty themes list; its first entry is the primary theme.
For each affected user/system flow, the count/ratio of member product capabilities matching the primary theme is reported (source: most should match).
verification: A check reads each affected user/system flow: a missing or empty explicit themes list is flagged as a violation, not treated as unknown or exempt.
The check reads the first declared theme as the primary theme; the general standard for alignment is 'most', not 'all', product capabilities matching.

The check reports, per affected user/system flow, the count or ratio of member product capabilities matching the primary theme; it reads 'most' as more than half for reporting, invents no stricter threshold, and does not present majority alignment as this rule's mandatory gate (the source strength is 'should'; explicit declaration is the mandatory part).

Recheck scope: every user/system flow whose membership changed - including the user/system flow a moved or removed product capability left - and every user/system flow containing a product capability whose theme changed, not only user/system flows whose own artifact changed.

User/system flow and product capability definition files are identified by path or kind in the planning area; this rule mandates no specific location (its reference realization states none), and product capability files are read because a product capability's theme and membership feed its user/system flow's theme fit.
Theme-name canonicality is not checked by this rule; it is covered by the sibling canonicality convention.

values: user/system flow touched while lacking an explicit themes list
product capability added to or moved into a user/system flow
product capability removed from or moved out of a user/system flow (affects source and destination user/system flows)
user/system flow themes list added, removed, changed or reordered
theme of an existing member product capability changed (in the product capability artifact or elsewhere)
user/system flow has a missing or empty explicit themes list
most of a user/system flow's member product capabilities are off the primary (first declared) theme

fires: Planner creates a new user/system flow and assigns product capabilities to it
Planner touches a user/system flow that has no explicit themes list (missing declaration must be fixed, not skipped)
Planner adds or moves product capabilities into an existing user/system flow whose primary theme differs from the new product capabilities' theme
Planner removes a product capability from a user/system flow, or moves a product capability out of one user/system flow into another (both user/system flows are rechecked)
Planner reorders a user/system flow's themes list, changing which theme is primary
Planner changes the theme of an existing product capability that belongs to a user/system flow, even when the user/system flow artifact itself is not edited
doesNotFire: Editing a product capability's acceptances without changing its theme or user/system flow membership
Editing code or tests outside planning artifacts
Validating that a theme name is canonical (covered by planner.theme.must-be-canonical)

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact kinds that are the user/system flow and product capability definition files this rule reads; the activation fact file_kind takes its values from these kinds (product capability files matter because a product capability's theme and membership feed its user/system flow's theme fit).

neutralityNotes: Trains, wagons and themes are shared planning-model concepts, not stack terms, so given/when/then/why, prefer, avoid, unless and evidence carry over essentially verbatim; the core names no stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, suffix or path. The only realization-specific content is the concrete source examples (verifier_detail[1], verifier_detail[2]) and this rule's term/finding/detector ids, all marked bunOnly; core:verification names the checks generically. The cross-reference to planner.theme.must-be-canonical in doesNotFire is a catalog-level rule id, kept as-is (this rule's legacyId equals its PLT-87 id, so catalog ids are shared across realizations). bun.json states no concrete location for train and wagon definition files, so no path profile requirement is made: only roles.plan_artifact.kinds is required, and the source's generic path/kind identification note is retained in core:verification. No vocabulary key was missing, so proposedKeys is empty.
